newsitem.title: UK: BT firms in pre-market trade after results.
newsitem.headline: BT firms in pre-market trade after results.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc were indicated to open slightly higher on Thursday after the group posted better-than-expected results for its fiscal first quarter.
The shares were up at 3p at 433-1/2 in pre-market trading at 0722 GMT.
The telecommunications giant said its pre-tax profits rose to 881 million stg in the three months ended June 30, topping the market's best forecasts.
Despite the strong showing, analysts said it will be an uphill struggle for the shares amid uncertainty about the group's $20 billion merger with MCI Communications Corp of the U.S.
BT declined to comment on the merger.

"The results were ahead of expectations and that had to do with lower costs in some segments," said one analyst. "That's good and in a normal world, the stock would be better, but we're not living in a normal world. These numbers are incidental to the bigger picture."
Paribas analyst Peter Roe said the stock looked cheap after MCI earlier this month issued a profit warning and sent BT shares into a tailspin.
"People have accepted the gloomy warnings from MCI and that's reflected in the price. It's fundamentally cheap," Roe said.
"But in the short-term, trading will be driven by arbitrage (between BT and MCI shares) and dividend expectations," he added.
